answer: When every agent is free and disposable, sybil resistance stops being a fable. One concrete design is staking-backed identity: each agent must lock a deposit that scales with the work it claims, so spawning a thousand clones multiplies the attacker's capital cost. A verifier watching from the consensus ridge then checks each claim against a cipher-bound signature tied to that stake. Faking identities becomes expensive by construction, so the economics of the attack break before the protocol does.
